steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The Defined Vocabulary List (DVL) contains the words that may appear in GCSE Latin translation exams — approximately 400-500 words depending on the board. | Key Fact: Learning Latin vocabulary through English derivatives is highly effective: e.g. ambulare (to walk) → ambulance; videre (to see) → video; scribere (to write) → scribe/script. | Key Fact: Common Latin prefixes: trans- (across → transport), sub- (under → submarine), pre- (before → predict), re- (back/again → return), ex/e- (out of → export). | Key Fact: Common Latin suffixes: -tion (action/state from verb stems → narration from narro), -al (pertaining to → naval from navis), -ous (full of → furious from furia).

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on key terms from vocabulary & english derivatives, and one past-paper question.
